model: winged zebrafish - zebrafish with the pectoral fin proportion moved toward the flying fish
units_and_axes: glTF Y-up; head at +X, back at +Y, the fish's left side at -Z. The adult / resolved set has SL = 0.82 model units; earlier growth stages are built at their TRUE relative size SL(age)/SL(adult), so development plays as real growth. standard_length_m = 0.0388 m sets the metres per model unit.
MORPHOLOGICAL_NOT_GENETIC: MORPHOLOGICAL edit, not a genetic modification. This design is ONE parent (zebrafish-adult) with its parameters moved by the named deltas; a delta is a change to a shape, not an allele, a pathway or a developmental programme, and nothing here says such an animal could be bred, is viable or is developmentally reachable. This is a shape, not an organism.
generative_model: parameters = SUM over parents ( weight_i * parent_i.parameter ) + delta

lean_recheck.why: a design inherits whatever constraints its parents satisfy; every delta needs re-checking

standard_length_m.drives: real-world standard length; sets the metres-per-model-unit scale

body_mass_kg.drives: wet mass; with flight_muscle_fraction sets the girdle muscle volume

body_depth_over_SL.drives: maximum body depth / SL (full depth, not half)

body_section_exponent.drives: superellipse exponent of the trunk cross-section (2 = ellipse)

head_fraction_SL.drives: fraction of SL over which the snout rounds off

peduncle_depth_frac.drives: caudal peduncle depth / maximum body depth

peduncle_width_frac.drives: caudal peduncle width / maximum body width

pectoral_len_over_SL.drives: longest pectoral fin ray, base to tip, / SL

delta.reason: a chosen point between the zebrafish placeholder (0.155) and the flying-fish measured median (0.687), near the flying-halfbeak median 0.274-0.388 (Daane groups). Chosen, not measured.

pectoral_span_over_SL.drives: pectoral tip-to-tip span / SL (both fins, across the body)

pectoral_area_over_SL2.drives: area of BOTH pectoral fins together / SL^2 (Park & Choi 2010 A1 = planform area of the pectoral fin PAIR; their mean chord c = A1/S over the full span S confirms A1 covers both fins)

delta.reason: area follows length^1.834 (Davenport 1992 exponent, development/trajectory.mjs P.area.exp); an assumed transfer from flying fish to zebrafish

pectoral_ray_count.drives: lepidotrichia per pectoral fin (one named mesh each)

flight_muscle_fraction.drives: pectoral/girdle muscle mass / body mass; sets the VOLUME of pectoral_muscle_L/R, so it visibly thickens the girdle musculature

mesh_detail.drives: global mesh resolution multiplier (1.0 = the committed flying-fish detail)

derived_from_the_mesh.flight_muscle_note: the pectoral girdle musculature is sized by VOLUME from flight_muscle_fraction x body_mass, then clipped to what fits inside the skin. fit_fraction < 1 means the requested muscle mass does not fit in this body at this schematic geometry.
derived_from_the_mesh.measured_how: areas are membrane surface areas measured on the exported mesh; span is the tip-to-tip extent of the pectoral fins in the spanwise axis. The physical values use standard_length_m / 0.8200 model units.

definitions.pectoral_aspect_ratio: = span2_over_area_both (kept under this name for existing readers): tip-to-tip pectoral span^2 / area of BOTH pectoral fins together. This IS the Park & Choi 2010 convention, AR = S^2/A1 with A1 the planform area of the fin pair (L3: 0.261^2/0.006377 = 10.68). Before 2.0.0 this text wrongly said 'area of ONE fin'; the number was always the both-fins arithmetic.
definitions.span2_over_area_both: tip-to-tip pectoral span^2 / area of BOTH pectoral fins together = Park & Choi 2010 AR (S^2/A1)
definitions.aspect_ratio_one_fin: (span/2)^2 / (area of ONE pectoral fin) = span2_over_area_both / 2: one fin treated as a wing from the body midline to its tip. No fetched source uses it; it is here so 'one-fin AR' has one unambiguous meaning. NOTE span^2 / one-fin area (= 2 x Park & Choi) matches no source and is not stored.
definitions.span2_over_wing_area_fish1990: tip-to-tip pectoral span^2 / (both pectoral + both pelvic fin areas): Fish 1990's AR, whose 'wing area' is pectoral + pelvic fins plus the body rectangles between each fin pair (J Zool 221:391, Methods). The body rectangles are not modelled, so this is an UPPER BOUND on the Fish-1990 value. Fish's 3.0-16.9 range is in this convention, not Park & Choi's.
definitions.lifting_area_m2: pectoral (both) + pelvic (both) + caudal membrane area measured on the mesh. NOTE: physics/flier's reference area 0.012688 m2 is Park & Choi's A = A1 + A2 + A3, where A3 = 0.004474 m2 is the BODY planform, not the caudal fin; the mesh's caudal membrane stands in for A3 here (see CHANGELOG 2.0.0, open item)
definitions.flight_muscle_volume_m3: flight_muscle_fraction * body_mass / 1060 kg/m3 (teleost muscle density, assumed)

derived_from_the_mesh.aspect_ratio_note: pectoral_aspect_ratio == span2_over_area_both == Park & Choi 2010's AR = S^2/A1 (A1 = BOTH pectoral fins; the L3 fish is 10.68). aspect_ratio_one_fin = (S/2)^2 / one fin's area = half of it. span2_over_wing_area_fish1990 divides by pectoral + pelvic area, Fish 1990's 'wing area' without the body rectangles between the fins, so it is an upper bound on a Fish-1990 AR; Fish's 3.0-16.9 range is in that convention. Definitions and evidence: design-schema.json aspect_ratio_conventions.

parameter_vs_mesh_check.what: the parameters ask for a span and an area; these are what the exported MESH actually has
parameter_vs_mesh_check.verdict: NO FIT was applied: the pectoral geometry is driven by pectoral_len_over_SL (this is what keeps the reference faithful to the committed flying-fish.glb). The span and area parameters are therefore TARGETS THAT THE MESH DOES NOT MEET, and the ratios above say by how much. For the flying fish this exposes a real discrepancy: the committed mesh's pectoral membrane is much broader (lower aspect ratio) than the Park & Choi 2010 specimen it is compared with. Note the measured value is a projected planform area while the mesh value is membrane surface area, which accounts for a few per cent, not for a factor of two.

morph_targets.note: the resolved parameter set 'winged-zebrafish' itself; weight 1 here = the adult / design as built. Stage targets' size_rel is relative to THIS SL.

morph_target_rule: set the weights of the two bracketing targets to (1-f, f) and every other target to 0; weights always sum to 1. See anatomy-model/parametric/INTEGRATION.md.

inside_check.what: superellipse norm of every internal piece against the skin surface; <= the piece's limit means it does not poke outside

layers: outer (skin, eyes, fin membranes) / muscle / skeleton / organ

design_record.name: winged zebrafish - zebrafish with the pectoral fin proportion moved toward the flying fish

real_experimental_counterpart.what: the germline lat4a nr21/+ ; kcnh2a lof/+ double heterozygote (genotype/compare-2x2.json panel B)
real_experimental_counterpart.caveat: This is the closest real experiment, and its paired-fin measurements exist ONLY in figure panels (Fig. 4B pectoral fin length): no numeric value appears in the paper's text, legends or Data S1, and nothing is digitised here. So the 0.35 below is NOT that experiment's number; it is a chosen point between the zebrafish placeholder and the flying-fish median. The real fish's fins are described as 'overgrown', with medial fins wild-type-sized and the caudal hypocercal.

pectoral_len_over_SL.reason: a chosen point between the zebrafish placeholder (0.155) and the flying-fish measured median (0.687), near the flying-halfbeak median 0.274-0.388 (Daane groups). Chosen, not measured.

pectoral_area_over_SL2.reason: area follows length^1.834 (Davenport 1992 exponent, development/trajectory.mjs P.area.exp); an assumed transfer from flying fish to zebrafish
